analysis: Docs-only PR. identity-binding.md adds (1) head lines ~94-111: App Attest same-process endpoint resumption. A provider responder uses the in-memory NodeKeyPair, with a protocol-1 transcript bound to a socket nonce, and writes directly to the socket. The docs state no local trust is created and no proof lifetime is extended, and that retained-proof, account, revocation and authorization checks are backend-owned and may not be deployed. (2) head lines ~137-144: provider logout revokes the saved token via raw-bearer POST /v1/device/revoke and warns that offline logout cannot invalidate copies. attestation.md (units :6/:7) was shown as full head text without a visible diff. I reviewed it for consistency with TB-009/TB-011. The legacy cohort policy, routing gate and invariants text looks consistent with the base model, and I found no contradiction. The next pass should check the coordinator code for the resume challenge handler (nonce single-use, binding to connection and endpoint, revocation fence at inference_authorization.go authorizeInferenceHandoff) and the /v1/device/revoke handler (auth, rate limit, effect on live B6-bound connections). Neither is in the supplied sources. I filed two low gap findings, T-053/TB-011 and A-008 related; neither is a verified code regression.

findings.detail: The new identity-binding.md section documents a provider-side responder that answers a coordinator 'resume' challenge with the in-memory X25519 key. It also references backend 'retained-proof' checks that are 'platform-owned' and may not be deployed. This is a new way to re-establish a serving binding without a fresh Apple assertion. TB-011, T-053 (replayed proof or stale authorization after a connection change) and T-057 do not describe it. Nothing in the model covers the nonce and socket binding, single use, the retained-proof lifetime limit, the revocation fence, or the case where a provider ships the responder before the coordinator counterpart exists. A stale or replayed resume challenge on a replacement socket, or a retained proof outliving revocation, would extend serving authorization. Fix: add the resume path to TB-011 and T-053 with explicit invariants (fresh per-socket nonce, one answer, proof age cap, revocation and qualification-generation recheck at final handoff, no lease extension).
findings.title: App Attest same-process endpoint resumption is a new authorization-adjacent path outside the threat model

findings.detail: Provider logout now sends the raw bearer token to POST /v1/device/revoke. The docs say backend revocation policy and persistence are 'platform-owned' and that local deletion cannot invalidate a copy held elsewhere, with an offline warning. This adds an unauthenticated-by-session bearer-in-request control-plane endpoint and a state where a deleted token stays valid on the coordinator. A thief holding a copied provider token (A-008) can keep registering as that account's provider, and the endpoint itself could be abused to revoke tokens if the token is leaked. The model has no threat for provider-token lifecycle: revoke endpoint rate-limiting, token-in-body or header logging, revocation idempotency, immediate effect on live connections bound by B6, and what happens when offline logout leaves the token active. Fix: add a threat and mitigations for A-008 token revocation, including terminating or rebinding existing sessions on revocation.
findings.title: New provider-token revocation endpoint and logout flow are not covered by the threat model
